title: An Empirical Study on the Impact of Normalized Use-Case Specifications on Traceability
abstract: arXiv:2608.15726v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Traceability link recovery between requirements and source code is vital for software quality assurance and evolution analysis. Although automated traceability techniques have advanced greatly, the large semantic gap between vague natural-language requirements and precise source code still hinders accurate link recovery. Most existing approaches optimize traceability algorithms yet ignore the inherent quality of requirement descriptions, which prevents fundamental reduction of the semantic gap. This work proposes a requirement-oriented normalization method. Using controlled natural language and large-language-model-based prompt engineering, raw requirements are decomposed and converted into standardized use-case specifications to strengthen semantic representation and mitigate semantic divergence. Evaluated on four public datasets under two typical traceability frameworks, the normalized specifications improve tracing performance for sem

translated_title: 规范化用例规格对可追溯性影响的经验研究
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.15726v1 公告类型：新 摘要：需求和源代码之间的可追溯性链接恢复对于软件质量保证和演化分析至关重要。尽管自动化可追溯性技术已取得显著进展，但模糊的自然语言需求与精确的源代码之间巨大的语义鸿沟仍然阻碍着准确的链接恢复。大多数现有方法优化了可追溯性算法，却忽视了需求描述本身的质量，这无法从根本上缩小语义差距。本工作提出了一种面向需求的规范化方法。利用受控自然语言和基于大型语言模型的提示工程，将原始需求分解并转换为标准化的用例规格，以加强语义表示并缓解语义分歧。在四个公开数据集上，在两种典型的可追溯性框架下进行评估，规范化规格提高了半自动可追溯性性能。
tldr: 本研究提出一种面向需求的规范化方法，通过受控自然语言和大型语言模型将原始需求转换为标准化用例规格，有效缩小语义鸿沟并提升可追溯性链接恢复性能。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a requirement-oriented normalization method that converts raw requirements into standardized use-case specifications using controlled natural language and large language models, effectively reducing the semantic gap and improving traceability link recovery performance.
